notes: The Skerrow's high roads and passes (docs/WORLD_LIFE_ROADS.md). Clanless and the Unroped at the passes and bridges, scree-hags on the gorge sides, crag-wolves and a stone-thrall crossing at night; on the road by day the clans' own traffic: memory-keepers walking to the Moot, Rudd carrying blood-price to the Stones, Skarl drovers, a tinker off the Oskel Edge camp. Caravans: Kharrow's pack train to Ruddow, Brindlecrag's ore carts to the Hold, and a Skarl pack train down from Skarlow.

lines.speaker: A clanless raider
lines.spring: No clan, no toll-stone, no mercy.

name: The Unroped's price
notes: Old Ghastow's people out on the road. The bait is one of them, a broken chain round his neck, who asks what you owe.

folk.name: A man with a broken chain

talk.prompt: Ask the man with the broken chain what he wants

lines.speaker: One of the Unroped
lines.spring: What are you worth? Nobody? Then nobody's owed for you.

name: Stones from above
notes: Scree-hags on the gorge side: the stones come first, from above, to find out whether you are the sort who looks up.

lines.speaker: A scree-hag
lines.spring: Look up. Look up. Look up.

name: A thrall carrying
notes: A stone-thrall crossing the road in the dark with a bone in its arms, going toward the Sorting Ground; it wants to be let past.

talk.prompt: Walk a way with the memory-keeper
talk.say: I am walking the Rope-Song to the Moot. Every verse, every name in it, from the Dreugh door to the Skarl fold. You may walk with me for a verse or two, if you do not talk. — There is a place up there the song goes quiet over. Go and look at it, if you like. I will not.

hook.rumour: The memory-keeper's song went quiet over {place}.

name: Blood-price on the road
notes: Two Rudd carrying a clan's blood-price to the Stones on the North Road, in plain sight, as the law says it is paid.

talk.prompt: Ask the Rudd what they carry
talk.say: A death's price, to the Stones, on the road where everyone can see. That is the point of the road. — Nine head and a year's peat, the reckoner said. We are carrying the coin for the peat. The beasts are walking on their own, behind, slower.

hook.rumour: The price-bearers came from the reckoner at {place}.

talk.say: Down the dale, and they know the way better than I do. Stand still till they're past, they don't like strangers standing in the middle of their road. — If you're going up Skarldale, water at the drove-well and ring the bell. Everything round there knows that note.
Mended pots, mended chains, mended news. The news is the dear one.
